jobs.title: 入り江の港
jobs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: one environment or scene illustration for the original exploration game "Ash Estuary"; wide landscape, approximately 16:9, edge-to-edge, opaque background.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved STYLE reference B. Match its actual fine pen contours, soft watercolor washes, restrained realistic observation, subtle warm paper grain, and material detail. It is a style reference; do not copy its water gate or net yard into a different location. If Image 2 is supplied it is a LOCATION/OBJECT continuity reference for this scene, not a second art style.
Art direction: Quiet, beautiful, slightly uneasy coastal life. Hand-drawn pen and pale watercolor, readable space, irregular fine lines, restrained cross-hatching, delicate gray-blue atmospheric distance. Chalk-white and warm-ivory limestone, slate-gray water and sky, muted moss and blue-green, weathered brown wood and small rust accents. Soft overcast daylight, legible shadows, no crushed black or saturated cinema grading. Keep the detailed observational character of reference B rather than flattening it or switching to an oil painting.
World and visual invariants: Small preindustrial coastal settlement; ordinary human-scale architecture and maintenance. Labor and everyday materials carry the story. Memory stones have no visible readable memories or supernatural glow. No ghosts, flashbacks inside stones, restored memories, giant castles, modern machinery, monsters, fighting, magical birds, bodily corrosion, or apocalyptic destruction. No readable words, numerals, labels, arrows, captions, UI, border or watermark. Written records use indistinct pen strokes. Avoid hero poses; named character designs are not fixed, so people are small figures or cropped hands without distinctive faces.
Scene/backdrop: The central harbor of the estuary, at the start of the journey. Human-scale white-stone waterfront warehouses used by the bell keepers, a modest stone landing and a moored working sailboat. Weathered wooden doors, rope coils and an ordinary workbench with unmarked cloth sacks ready for allocation. The gray estuary opens beyond; pale coastal slopes recede into overcast air.
Subject and framing: A wide grounded view from the quay. Warehouse and workbench in the near middle-ground, landing and water beyond. A couple of very small local workers quietly carry out routine harbor work. The white stone, repaired walls and hand-tended equipment should feel like the same settlement as reference B.
Narrative constraints: An arrival scene, no revealed experiment, no tragic or successful outcome, no fixed inventory counts displayed. Sacks look like ordinary materials, not glowing magical containers. This is the CENTRAL HARBOR, not the southern sluice; do not include the circular cistern or net racks from the style reference.

Scene/backdrop: The northern white-limestone quarry above the same gray estuary. A handsome but human-scale white-stone stair descends from a small outlook. Behind the stair, partly visible from this oblique angle, is a compact masonry firing kiln on a worn elevated stone base supported by plain timber props; the improvised props communicate ongoing maintenance. An open stone-lined delivery channel leads toward a small local northern sluice near a humble washing place, away from the southern water gate.
Subject and framing: Wide establishing view from beside the stone stair, looking across the working quarry and down toward the estuary. Calm white steps draw the eye through the image; the kiln and timber support base are distinct in the middle-ground. A few small anonymous work figures quietly attend the site, with no emphasized faces.
Narrative constraints: BEFORE repairs. The kiln base is still propped with wood; the beautiful stair has modest wear and an obscured chipped underside, not collapse. Leave the delivery-channel problem visually unobtrusive at arrival; no tracer demonstration yet. Ordinary quarry and kiln, no giant industrial factory, spectacular fire, castle or southern circular cistern. This view will serve as the location continuity reference for later quarry scenes.
